http_semantics.note: No 2xx masking: every invalid peer-id form was rejected. Two distinct 4xx conventions coexist: request-side-decidable parse errors (alpha/float/overflow) surface as HTTP 404 with a plain-text framework message (routing-level semantics - unparseable path segment treated as unmatched route), while the application-level refusal (ghost u64) surfaces as HTTP 400 with the qdrant business envelope {"status":{"error":...}}; the 404-for-parse-error status choice is itself part of the diagnostics observation

chain_trace.break_detail: Broken at the doc link: the contract's negative-branch promise ('4xx on an invalid peer id') is not documentation prose - the remove-peer page documents only the 200 response and 'returns an error if the node (peer) has shards on it' - so the promise cannot be traced to the cited source. Additionally, the Type-2 diagnostic-quality rubric that produced the verdict exists only in the script (neither contract nor doc asserts anything about error-message quality), so the verdict's standard of comparison is test-side. The contract->script->log links themselves are intact and consistent: the 4xx the assertion promises was in fact delivered, and the log says so explicitly ('the 4xx is delivered but undiagnosable').

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: Two disjoint paths produce the observed rejections. (a) Malformed peer_id: DELETE /cluster/peer/{peer_id} route (cluster_api.rs:75) declares peer_id: web::Path<u64> (line 78) - the PLAIN actix-web extractor; a non-u64 segment fails extraction inside actix-web 4.13.0 (Cargo.lock:231) before the handler runs, and actix-web's default extractor-error response is HTTP 404 with the plain-text deserialization message 'can not parse "X" to a u64' (the string has ZERO hits anywhere in the qdrant tree - it is dependency-origin, not a qdrant-authored diagnostic). (b) Well-formed ghost u64: extraction succeeds, toc.peer_has_shards(ghost)=false, then dispatcher.consensus_state() returns None on this single-node deployment, yielding StorageError::bad_request("Distributed mode disabled.") (cluster_api.rs:108-110), Display-formatted 'Bad request: {description}' (lib/storage/src/content_manager/errors.rs:26-27, constructor :65), mapped by ResponseError to HTTP 400 (src/actix/helpers.rs:242-248) inside the qdrant business envelope. The diagnostics gap is structural and verifiable in first-party source: src/actix/mod.rs:105-106 registers actix_web_validator::PathConfig with validation_error_handler("path parameters", ...) (app_data at :142), whose output names the parameter section ('Validation error in path parameters: ...' / 'Deserialize error in path parameters: ...', mod.rs:227-247) - but a repo-wide grep for 'validator::Path' returns exactly ONE hit, the registration itself; no route in the codebase uses actix_web_validator::Path (all twelve path extractors in src/actix/api/*.rs are plain web::Path), so the application's own diagnostic handler for path parameters is unreachable, and every path-parse failure including this one falls through to the framework default. Neither message names the parameter subject 'peer' together with an actionable hint, matching the rubric scores 0/3-1/3. No explicit by-design annotation (comment/docstring/maintainer note) exists for the message quality, so by_design_in_source is not claimable.

mundane_explanation.surviving: deployment-mode gating of the 400 leg only: the sandbox runs qdrant single-node (consensus off), so the well-formed-ghost probe's message is 'Distributed mode disabled.' rather than a peer-specific error; on a distributed deployment that one leg would surface different content (propose_consensus_op_with_await path). The three parse-404 legs and the rubric best=1/3 are mode-independent framework behavior, so the Type-2 observation itself survives this explanation.
